vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.name: La Osa Data Center Park
vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.powered_by: WAPA grid interconnect; on-site natural gas (phase 1); solar (planned)
vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.utility: Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) — proposed grid transmission line upgrades for interconnect. APS and SRP not confirmed as utility providers.
vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.water_notes: Developer's attorney stated commitment to air-cooled or closed-loop cooling to minimize water demand. Site borders the Greene Canal, raising concerns about water access and consumption in an arid region. No MGD figures have been published. Critics cited Pima County's 'Project Blue' hyperscale data center as a cautionary precedent for water misuse in Arizona desert developments.
vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.source: Land developer Vermaland pitches $33bn data center in Arizona
vermaland-la-osa-eloy-az.notes: Vermaland LLC is a Phoenix-area land developer and land-banking company (CEO Kuldip 'Ken' Verma, founded 2006, controls ~25,000 acres of metro Phoenix land). DCD explicitly noted 'it is unclear whether Vermaland would operate its own data center facilities' — Vermaland plans to sell or rent parcels/buildings to tenants. No end tenants or hyperscaler operators have been named as of July 2026. Original plan: 59 data centers, up to 3 GW capacity ceiling, up to $33B investment ceiling, 3,300-acre site south of Eloy along the Greene Canal. A separate adjacent 1,700-acre parcel already holds Industrial-2 zoning for data centers, gas plants, battery storage, and solar. After strong public opposition (all ~60 public comments opposed), operator announced May 2026 scale-back to 11 data centers and 1 GW ceiling. Board of Supervisors hearing scheduled August 26, 2026; no permits issued as of record date. Site lies adjacent to a Qualified Opportunity Zone (investor tax benefit; not a direct subsidy to Vermaland — no subsidy award confirmed, omitted). Coordinates are approximate (parcel south of Eloy city center along Greene Canal; no precise APN published). $33B investment and all GW figures are announced ceilings, not firm commitments.

microsoft-goodyear-az.name: Microsoft Goodyear Data Center Campus
microsoft-goodyear-az.water_notes: Microsoft updated development agreement requiring 4th and 5th buildings to use air cooling rather than direct evaporative cooling originally intended. Contributing nearly $42M total: $36M to expand 157th Ave Wastewater Treatment Plant (of a planned $90M expansion), $5M financial assurance toward dedicated sewer line, $800K city coordinator fee.
microsoft-goodyear-az.source: Microsoft purchases 100 acres next to Goodyear campus
microsoft-goodyear-az.notes: Near Citrus and Indian School roads, Goodyear (address: 3785 Citrus Rd per industry sources). Two-million sq ft of existing or under-construction data centers. investmentUsd is reported campus value; land-only spend is additional. Coordinates approximate; exact site is west Goodyear near airport. First land purchase corrected to April 2019 / 150 acres / $37.11M per DCD primary source; intermediate purchases brought pre-2025 footprint to approximately 450 acres before the 100-acre 2025 expansion to 550+ total.

prologis-silver-creek-valley-san-jose-ca.name: Prologis Silver Creek Valley Road Data Center
prologis-silver-creek-valley-san-jose-ca.source: Prologis files to build 99MW data center in San Jose, California
prologis-silver-creek-valley-san-jose-ca.notes: 5977 Silver Creek Valley Road, South San Jose. Three-story facility, 516,000 sq ft. Permit filed July 2026; ~2-year buildout once approved. Prologis states it will self-fund substation/transmission costs. Distinct from Prologis's already-tracked Project Sail, Project Cardinal, and Project Mila entries. Coordinates are approximate.

ne-edge-millstone-ct.name: NE Edge Millstone Nuclear Data Center
ne-edge-millstone-ct.source: Millstone Nuclear Plant Would Power Proposed CT Data Center
ne-edge-millstone-ct.notes: Connecticut has no hyperscale data centers. Governor Lamont's administration has since required new data centers to bring their own power generation rather than draw from the grid, and has proposed a PILOT framework in lieu of the prior tax incentive structure. Only one company (Cigna) used Connecticut's data center tax incentive since its enactment.

coresite-or1-orlando-fl.name: CoreSite OR1 — Orlando
coresite-or1-orlando-fl.source: CoreSite looks to add second Orlando data center building
coresite-or1-orlando-fl.notes: 129,000 sq ft colocation facility on a 16-acre campus at 9701 S John Young Pkwy (rebranded from DataSite in 2022). A ~76,280 sq ft second building is proposed, with an ERP modification filed May 2026.

microsoft-douglasville-ga.name: Microsoft Douglasville Data Center Campus
microsoft-douglasville-ga.powered_by: Georgia Power grid (Douglas County service area)
microsoft-douglasville-ga.water_notes: The Douglasville–Douglas County Water & Sewer Authority (Dog River Reservoir) is the provider; no facility-specific water volume is published. Microsoft pledges to be 'water positive' by 2030 and reports an 80%+ reduction in water intensity company-wide.
microsoft-douglasville-ga.source: Microsoft to launch new cloud region in Atlanta, Georgia, in 2027
microsoft-douglasville-ga.notes: Four 245,000 sq ft technology facilities totaling ~980,000 sq ft on 160-acre parcel at 1601 North River Road, Douglasville. Part of Azure East US 3 region alongside facilities in East Point and Palmetto. Coordinates are Douglasville city centroid; actual site is northern Douglasville.

eagle-rock-meridian-technology-park-tayl.name: Meridian Technology Park
eagle-rock-meridian-technology-park-tayl.source: Eagle Rock Partners Proposes $8.8B, 1GW Data Center Campus in Christian County, Illinois
eagle-rock-meridian-technology-park-tayl.notes: Proposed 475-acre, 10-building (100MW each, ~1,000MW total) data center campus in unincorporated Christian County, ~2 miles southwest of Taylorville near Clarksdale. Estimated cost $6B-$8.8B. Earliest construction would not begin before 2028-2029. No formal application had been filed with the county as of the board's first briefing on the proposal; zoning board and county board votes are still pending. Not yet listed on major public data center trackers.

tenkey-franklin-ky.name: TenKey LandCo Project Lionsgate – Franklin Data Center
tenkey-franklin-ky.source: Second lawsuit filed over proposed data center in Simpson County
tenkey-franklin-ky.notes: Site: 421 Steele Road (Steele Road near Exit 2 on I-65), Franklin, Simpson County, KY. Coordinates are approximate for that I-65 exit area within Franklin city limits. Three 200,000 sq ft buildings plus on-site natural gas power generation planned. End hyperscaler not publicly identified; Simpson County Judge-Executive Mason Barnes refused to sign NDA and called the pitch full of red flags. Data center opposition became a factor in May 2026 local primary elections in Simpson County. Fix: investmentUsd corrected from $1.6B to $4.8B — LPM confirms total project is 'nearly $5 billion'; the $1.6B figure in the original record is the per-building cost (each of three 200,000 sq ft facilities costs approximately $1.6B, totaling ~$4.8B).

servistar-westfield-ma.name: Servistar Realties Westfield Data Center Campus
servistar-westfield-ma.notes: Would-be first Massachusetts hyperscale data center: 10-building, 2.7M sq ft campus over a long buildout (191/199 Servistar Industrial Way). Tax exemption secured 2024. Status is early and thin — no confirmed groundbreaking; conflicting signals on whether the project is still active.

aligned-quantum-frederick-md.name: Aligned Data Centers IAD-04 Frederick
aligned-quantum-frederick-md.water_notes: Aligned describes "Delta³ air cooling arrays" plus "DeltaFlow liquid cooling" within a "closed-loop chilled water system" and markets "near-zero water consumption"; no facility MGD disclosed. Cooling spec is campus-level and may not be IAD-04-specific.
aligned-quantum-frederick-md.source: Aligned breaks ground on 72MW Maryland data center in Quantum Frederick Park
aligned-quantum-frederick-md.notes: Part of TPG Real Estate / Catellus Development's 2,100-acre Quantum Frederick campus on former Alcoa Eastalco aluminum plant (closed 2010, demolished 2017) in Frederick County MD. Coordinates are approximate for campus area near Buckeystown/Adamstown.

terawulf-morgantown-charles-county-md.name: TeraWulf Morgantown Generating Station AI Campus
terawulf-morgantown-charles-county-md.source: TeraWulf buys Maryland coal plant to fuel AI data centers
terawulf-morgantown-charles-county-md.notes: Morgantown Generating Station is on the Potomac River near the Governor Harry W. Nice Memorial Bridge, Charles County MD. Acquisition funding and TeraWulf financial stability questioned by Maryland Office of People's Counsel (net losses $660M+ in 2025, 90% revenue from Bitcoin mining). Coordinates approximate. TeraWulf sought about $100M in Maryland state funds toward the Morgantown acquisition; the purchase price is withheld from FERC as confidential (FOIA Exemption 4), which Public Citizen is petitioning to disclose. No cooling design, water-withdrawal figure, confirmed subsidy, or job count has been publicly disclosed for the proposed AI campus.

switch-pyramid-campus-grand-rapids-mi.name: Switch Pyramid Campus
switch-pyramid-campus-grand-rapids-mi.water_notes: No facility-specific cooling type or water volume is disclosed; the City of Grand Rapids provides water and sewer service.
switch-pyramid-campus-grand-rapids-mi.source: Switch plans second expansion of pyramid data center campus in Grand Rapids, Michigan
switch-pyramid-campus-grand-rapids-mi.notes: Steelcase Pyramid campus, Gaines Township, Kent County MI (south of Grand Rapids; NOT the city of Wyoming, which is a separate municipality ~5 km north). Total campus target: 1.8M sq ft, 320 MW, ~$5B investment across all phases. Phase 1 (225,000 sq ft white space) and Phase 2 (312,000 sq ft) operational; Phase 3 in planning/early construction as of 2025. Michigan's largest data center by capacity. Coordinates are approximate Pyramid campus location on East Paris Ave, Gaines Township.

google-spade-new-florence-mo.name: Google Project Spade Campus
google-spade-new-florence-mo.source: Google pledges $15bn investment in New Florence, Missouri
google-spade-new-florence-mo.notes: DISTINCT from aws-green-new-florence-mo (AWS Project Green): the two are on opposite sides of I-70 (Project Green north; Project Spade south, SE quadrant of the I-70/Hwy 19 interchange) - independently verified via DCD and Columbia Missourian. Site ~934 acres (~780 unincorporated + ~130 in New Florence). Developer: Related Digital. Campus targets 1.2 GW. INVESTMENT OMITTED: the $15B is Google's Missouri-STATEWIDE infrastructure pledge ('Google will invest $15 billion in building infrastructure in Missouri, including a data center in New Florence'); the campus itself is described only as 'multi-billion-dollar', so no firm campus investmentUsd is recorded. Amended from three buildings to two ~800,000 sq ft buildings; first operations targeted 2028. ~2,000 construction jobs and 'hundreds' of permanent jobs are projections (in notes, not jobs). Coordinates are an approximate site centroid (no verified parcel record).

nebius-independence-mo.name: Nebius AI Factory (Independence)
nebius-independence-mo.powered_by: Independence Power & Light (IPL); Blue Valley Power Plant on-site gas (from Oct 2027)
nebius-independence-mo.water_notes: Operator states closed-loop system uses water roughly comparable to a QuikTrip convenience store annually; significantly below typical open-loop data center cooling
nebius-independence-mo.source: Nebius breaks ground on gigawatt-scale AI factory in Independence, Missouri
nebius-independence-mo.notes: Nebius Group's (Nasdaq: NBIS) first gigawatt-scale US data center project. Located in Eastgate Commerce Center, off Little Blue Parkway and Missouri Highway 78 in eastern Independence. Up to 10 buildings planned. Phase 1 operational target Q2 2027; full campus completion 2028–2029. Projected $30–50M annual tax revenue for Independence. Separate Nebius facility exists at former Kansas City Star printing press building ~20 miles west (not this record). Coordinates approximate for Eastgate Commerce Center in eastern Independence. The $150.6B bond authorization is a Missouri Chapter 100 IDRB structure; bonds are privately issued and owned by Nebius — no city credit exposure.

aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms.name: AWS Project Atlas – Madison County Campus
aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms.water_notes: Canton facility transitioning to 100% recycled wastewater for cooling by 2027; 83 million gallons annually per Amazon announcement
aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms.source: AWS confirmed as company behind $10bn Mississippi data center development
aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms.notes: Two distinct complexes: Madison County Mega Site (outside Canton) and Costas Property (west of Tougaloo College near County Line Rd, Ridgeland). Amazon's total Mississippi statewide commitment expanded to $25B including subsequent Warren County ($3B) and Hinds County ($1B) announcements. Coordinates are approximate Canton-area centroid. Veolia water partnership claim removed: About Amazon source names Arable (not Veolia) as water replenishment partner; recycled wastewater target of 83M gallons/year by 2027 is confirmed.

google-lenoir-nc.name: Google Lenoir Data Center
google-lenoir-nc.source: Google Lenoir, North Carolina — official location page: announced 2007, opened 2008, ~$1.2B initial / $4B+ cumulative
google-lenoir-nc.notes: Google's flagship North Carolina data center in Lenoir, Caldwell County — announced 2007, operational since 2008, one of Google's earliest U.S. sites, expanded since. Per Google's own location page, the initial investment was ~$1.2B, with $4B+ invested in the region and state since. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the disclosed Lynhaven Dr address; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

impactdata-greensboro-nc.name: ImpactData Greensboro
impactdata-greensboro-nc.source: List of upcoming data centers in North Carolina
impactdata-greensboro-nc.notes: 20 MW facility in Greensboro, Guilford County, targeting mid-2026 completion. Single-tracker source → confidence reported. Coordinates are the Greensboro centroid.

google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed.name: Google Nebraska AI Campus (proposed)
google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed.water_notes: Cooling technology not disclosed in public filings. County officials and residents have raised concerns about combined water demand from the proposed data center and its associated natural-gas power plant.
google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed.source: Google proposes Nebraska data center requiring more power than all of Lincoln
google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed.notes: Exact site is unknown and undisclosed. Tenaska has optioned over 2,600 acres across Gage, Lancaster, Otoe, and Cass Counties in SE Nebraska since December 2025. Coordinates are approximate centroid of the Otoe/Gage County search area. Reported capacity range is 1,000–3,000 MW depending on phase; 1,000 MW used as minimum. Google has invested $3.5B in Nebraska since 2019 across existing Papillion, Omaha, and Lincoln data centers. Legislative feasibility depends on LB1261; could be operational by 2029 if approved.

google-papillion-ne.name: Google Papillion Data Center
google-papillion-ne.source: Google Nebraska — official location page: lists Papillion (2019), Omaha, and Lincoln as Google Nebraska data centers
google-papillion-ne.notes: Google data center at 14706 Schram Rd, Papillion, Sarpy County — announced Feb 2019 (built under shell entity Fireball Group LLC / 'Project Wizard'), a $600M project on ~275 acres, groundbreaking Oct 2019, operational ~2021. Confirmed by Google's own Nebraska location page (which lists Papillion, Omaha, and Lincoln as Google Nebraska sites). DISTINCT from the separate tracked proposed Google/Tenaska gas-plant project in SE Nebraska (Gage/Otoe area). No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the disclosed Schram Rd address; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

nebius-vineland-nj.name: Nebius Vineland Data Center
nebius-vineland-nj.water_notes: Developer explicitly states facility will not consume water for equipment cooling (Philadelphia Inquirer, Jan 2026). A four-step exhaust reclamation system on the gas engines (selective catalytic reduction, oxy catalyst, wet scrubbers, biofilters) captures condensate from engine exhaust for recycling — this is emissions control on the power plant side, not IT-equipment cooling. City department figures show 1.1 million gallons/year municipal water draw (Inquirer, Jan 2026); a separate source (WHYY) cites 'up to 20 million gallons annually' — discrepancy unresolved, likely reflecting different accounting (total throughput vs. net municipal draw). Reporting 'reportedMgd' field omitted due to conflicting figures.
nebius-vineland-nj.source: Nebius accelerates US expansion, adding up to 300 MW capacity at new data center in New Jersey
nebius-vineland-nj.notes: Phase-1 (~100 MW) completed summer 2025 in approximately 20 weeks from March 2025 announcement; full campus buildout targeting November 2026. Total design capacity cited as 'up to 300 MW' in Nebius press releases (sourceRef 0); DataOne CEO and local/community coverage consistently cite 350 MW; long-term campus potential described as approaching 1 GW. Coordinates are approximate (site: South Lincoln and Sheridan Avenues, East Vineland; Baxtel lists 805 Sheridan Ave). DataOne is the developer/builder — BSO's data center unit (launched 2024) backed by Ardian; CEO Charles-Antoine Beyney; this is DataOne's first US site (previously Grenoble and Lyon, France). Nebius is the ~10-year tenant; Microsoft GPU infrastructure agreement commencing late 2025 under multi-year AI infrastructure deal. Facility is 100% privately funded; DataOne declined a $6.2M city equipment loan amid community backlash. Distinct from Nebius's Independence, MO (Kansas City) site. NJDEP air permit pending as of early 2026; construction proceeded ahead of final permit issuance. DataOne stated 200+ permanent full-time jobs; construction job count not disclosed.

microsoft-fernley-nv.name: Microsoft Victory Logistics District Campus
microsoft-fernley-nv.source: Microsoft to buy 300 acres in Fernley's Lyon County Victory Logistics District
microsoft-fernley-nv.notes: ~300.7-acre land acquisition at the Victory Logistics District in Fernley, Lyon County. Capacity and timeline not yet announced → proposed. Coordinates are the Fernley area centroid.

aws-hayden-run-hilliard-oh.name: AWS Hayden Run Campus
aws-hayden-run-hilliard-oh.source: Franklin County Auditor parcel/GIS record (parcel 050-011444, 5109-5129 Hayden Run Rd — VADATA INC, land-use class 'data center', assessed building area 768,498 sq ft = built, 55.2 ac)
aws-hayden-run-hilliard-oh.notes: AWS's first US East (Ohio) region data center — a ~55-acre Vadata Inc campus at 5109-5129 Hayden Run Rd, Hilliard. Broke ground 2015; first building completed ~2018; a multi-building campus that has continued expanding. Franklin County Auditor land-use class 'data center' with 768,498 sq ft of assessed building area (= built/operational); owner Vadata Inc (Amazon's data-center subsidiary). Data-center directories (DC Byte / baxtel) list several numbered Hayden Run buildings (5109/5113/5117/5121/5125) that correspond to buildings within this single county parcel, not separate sites. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are the Franklin County Auditor parcel centroid. Distinct from the tracked AWS Cosgray Road and AWS Scioto Darby campuses (also Hilliard, Franklin County).

edgeconnex-ashville-oh.name: Ashville Campus
edgeconnex-ashville-oh.source: Proposed EdgeConneX data center in Pickaway County, Ohio facing criticism
edgeconnex-ashville-oh.notes: 680 acres north of SR-752; 1.8GW substation plus a 200MW gas turbine energy center planned. Facing local opposition/criticism.

cologix-col5-orange-township-delaware-co.name: Cologix COL5
cologix-col5-orange-township-delaware-co.source: Ohio Tax Credit Authority meeting action, June 1, 2026 (reported)
cologix-col5-orange-township-delaware-co.notes: Address 6787 Green Meadows Drive, Lewis Center OH 43035, southeast corner of Green Meadows Drive and Home Road, Orange Township. Power to be supplied by AEP. Phase 1 (135,000 sq ft, 25MW) construction began June 2025, targeted completion fall 2026; may expand to 75MW. Received 50%/10-year Ohio sales tax exemption (~$42.3M combined with the Licking County site) plus a 10-year 50% Delaware County property tax abatement, approved at the June 1, 2026 Ohio Tax Credit Authority meeting — the last such approval before Gov. DeWine's announced pause on new data center tax breaks. Coordinates are the Lewis Center/Orange Township town centroid, not parcel-verified in this session — recommend a follow-up parcel-level geocode of 6787 Green Meadows Drive before publishing at high precision.

strata-hanging-rock-haverhill-data-cente.name: Hanging Rock / Haverhill Data Center
strata-hanging-rock-haverhill-data-cente.source: Data center project in Lawrence County, Ohio sparks calls for moratorium in neighboring city
strata-hanging-rock-haverhill-data-cente.notes: At 1476 County Road 1A; land sold by the Lawrence County Economic Development Corp. Construction began around December 2025. A 5,178-signature opposition petition sparked a moratorium push in neighboring Ironton.

qts-new-albany-1-franklin-county-oh.name: QTS New Albany 1
qts-new-albany-1-franklin-county-oh.source: QTS plans four-building data center campus in New Albany, Ohio
qts-new-albany-1-franklin-county-oh.notes: 1225-1235 Beech Road SW, New Albany — in the Licking County section of the New Albany Business Park, the same submarket as CyrusOne's and Vantage's Licking County sites nearby. First of two adjacent QTS buildings (see also QTS New Albany 2); 885,600 sq ft. Combined QTS New Albany 1+2 investment ~$1.5B, enabled by a New Albany City Council Community Reinvestment Area tax agreement. 144MW is planned capacity; no operational MW disclosed. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found — QTS materials describe generic hyperscale/enterprise colo ("QTS Freedom Design").

stargate-lordstown-oh.name: Stargate Lordstown Campus
stargate-lordstown-oh.water_notes: SoftBank spokesperson: "The Lordstown site will also use a closed-loop cooling system that is designed to reduce water consumption." Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk (via AP): "These data centers are designed to not use water." No site-specific MGD figure published.
stargate-lordstown-oh.source: OpenAI, Oracle, and SoftBank expand Stargate with five new AI data center sites — OpenAI
stargate-lordstown-oh.notes: Planned 1,500 MW is a long-term campus ceiling, not a near-term operational figure: a SoftBank spokesperson said the initial SoftBank/OpenAI data center uses "a small part" of the 6.2M-sq-ft site, which also hosts a Foxconn/SoftBank hub manufacturing modular data-center equipment. Crescent Dune LLC (a SoftBank affiliate) acquired the site from Foxconn for $375M (Sept 2025, Trumbull County Auditor). SoftBank's "up to $3 billion" is a ceiling covering both manufacturing and the data center — no data-center-only investment figure is confirmed.

core-scientific-muskogee-ok.name: Core Scientific Muskogee Campus
core-scientific-muskogee-ok.source: Core Scientific Plans Expansion to 1.5 Gigawatts of Gross Power at Muskogee, Oklahoma Campus
core-scientific-muskogee-ok.notes: 1525 W Smith Ferry Rd, Port Muskogee Industrial Park. Distinct from the existing tracked Google Muskogee County campuses - same county, different developer/site. Coordinates are approximate.

beale-project-mustang-claremore-ok.name: Project Mustang
beale-project-mustang-claremore-ok.notes: Within Claremore Industrial Park. Distinct from Beale Infrastructure's tracked Owasso, OK site (Project Clydesdale, a different location).

meta-prineville-or.name: Meta Prineville Data Center Campus
meta-prineville-or.water_notes: Outdoor-air economizer cooling with evaporative assist on peak days. Annual withdrawal was ~68.4M gallons (2022), down from a ~117.5M-gallon peak (2020); use concentrates on roughly 10 hot summer days (about 10% of city consumption on those days). Meta co-funded a second aquifer storage-and-recovery injection well.

pennhurst-data-center-east-vincent-chest.name: Pennhurst Data Center Campus
pennhurst-data-center-east-vincent-chest.source: Pennhurst Data Center Developers Add 600,000 Square Feet, Gas Plant in Last-Minute Revision
pennhurst-data-center-east-vincent-chest.notes: ~1.9 million sq ft data center campus (five two-story buildings) on ~125 acres of the historic former Pennhurst State Hospital site in East Vincent Township, with a five-acre substation and an on-site 550 MW gas plant. Township denied conditional use; developer appealing in Chester County court.

hanton-city-smithfield-ri.name: Hanton City Business Park (data center anchor)
hanton-city-smithfield-ri.source: Proposed data center still looms over Smithfield, even after town council enacts ban
hanton-city-smithfield-ri.notes: No megawatt capacity has been publicly disclosed, so capacityMw is omitted. The $59M figure cited in coverage is projected town tax revenue over 30 years, not facility investment, so investmentUsd is not set. Additional coverage (Rhode Island Current, ecoRI News) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch and is not cited; the Ocean State Media article is the single independently verified resolvable source. Coordinates are approximate Smithfield-area coordinates.

cipher-stingray-andrews-county-tx.name: Cipher Stingray HPC Data Center
cipher-stingray-andrews-county-tx.source: Cipher Digital (Cipher Mining) FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-24) — Stingray Site, West Texas, conditional ERCOT interconnection up to 100 MW, energize H1 2026
cipher-stingray-andrews-county-tx.notes: Cipher's Stingray HPC/AI data center site, ~250 acres in Andrews County, Texas (west of the city of Andrews). Conditional ERCOT interconnection approval up to 100 MW; targeted energization H1/Q2 2026. Part of Cipher's ~3.4 GW / 8-site HPC pipeline. Cipher rebranded from Cipher Mining to Cipher Digital during its pivot to hyperscale HPC/AI hosting. Coordinates approximate (Andrews, TX geocode; exact parcel not confirmed).

google-meitner-pampa-tx.name: Google Meitner Energy Center
google-meitner-pampa-tx.water_notes: Air-cooling used in place of evaporative cooling to eliminate cooling-tower water withdrawals - a required condition of the Gray County Chapter 312 tax abatement. Ogallala Aquifer protection was the central abatement concern.
google-meitner-pampa-tx.source: Google and Intersect deepen Texas roots with new data center and energy investments in Gray and Roberts Counties
google-meitner-pampa-tx.notes: Data center co-located with new energy generation, spanning Gray and Roberts counties near Pampa. Part of Google's ~$40B Texas commitment; Google took a stake in Intersect Power. IT capacity not disclosed. Coordinates are the Pampa area centroid. Local reporting cites a ~$3B project cost (est. ~$1B/phase across 3 phases per the abatement filing) - an estimate -> investmentUsd omitted. ~40 permanent jobs projected across phases (abatement filing); facility not yet operational -> jobs honest-zero.

lambda-aligned-plano-tx.name: Lambda Plano AI Data Center (Aligned DFW-04)
lambda-aligned-plano-tx.source: Lambda Cloud to occupy Aligned data center in Plano
lambda-aligned-plano-tx.notes: Lambda to occupy the ~$700M Aligned DFW-04 data center under construction in Plano, Collin County; 2026 target. Distinct from Lambda's Chicago and Kansas City sites. Coordinates are the Plano area centroid.

meta-fort-worth-tx.name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center
meta-fort-worth-tx.source: Facebook Fort Worth Data Center — 4500 Like Way, opened 2017, ~200 acres, fully operational
meta-fort-worth-tx.notes: Meta (Facebook) data center at 4500 Like Way, Fort Worth, Tarrant County (near TX-170 and Park Vista Blvd) — broke ground 2015, began serving traffic in 2017, on a ~200-acre campus, heavily expanded since (with an announced AI-driven expansion). DISTINCT from Meta's tracked El Paso, TX campus. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the disclosed Like Way address; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

powerhouse-provident-grand-prairie-tx.name: PowerHouse Grand Prairie Campus
powerhouse-provident-grand-prairie-tx.source: PowerHouse and Provident to develop 1.8GW campus in DFW, Texas
powerhouse-provident-grand-prairie-tx.notes: 1.8 GW DFW-area campus (Grand Prairie): 24 buildings across three phases with an on-site 1.8 GW switchyard. Grand Prairie spans Dallas/Tarrant/Ellis counties; the campus is in the Ellis County (southern) portion. Coordinates reflect the southern Grand Prairie / Ellis County zone. Provident cited 'at least $5B in direct construction impact' over the multi-year build-out (Bisnow) and ~$300M for one 360,000-sq-ft building (Dallas Innovates) - neither a confirmed campus capex pledge -> investmentUsd omitted. Ellis County adopted Chapter 312 abatement guidelines (~Oct 2025, $50M threshold); no executed abatement agreement for this campus was found.

fermi-matador-amarillo-tx.name: Project Matador
fermi-matador-amarillo-tx.water_notes: No confirmed water use figures published. Community opposition raised concerns about Ogallala Aquifer impacts from combined cooling demand of gas plants and data centers. Arid Texas Panhandle location heightens water supply risk.
fermi-matador-amarillo-tx.source: Fermi America acquires 600MW of gas turbines for 11GW AI mega campus in Amarillo, Texas
fermi-matador-amarillo-tx.notes: 11GW is the long-term ceiling for the HyperGrid campus; near-term company targets include 1GW by end of 2026 and 2.3GW first-phase delivery — these are company goals, not firm commitments. Land acreage reported variously (5,769 acres per DCD July 2025 and 5,855 acres per other sources; later company materials cite 7,570 acres on 7,570 acres); using 5,769 as the earliest confirmed figure, sourced from the gas turbine acquisition announcement. Coordinates approximate (seed-provided; site in Carson County ~12 miles NE of Amarillo, adjacent to DOE Pantex Plant). Fermi America co-founded January 2025 by former Texas Governor and U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry, Toby Neugebauer (CEO, departed April 2026 after being fired 'without cause'), and Griffin Perry. IPO raised $682M on Nasdaq under ticker FRMI (October 2025), valuing company at ~$19B at opening; market cap collapsed to ~$3.4B by April 2026 after leadership exits and loss of anchor tenant ($150M LOI canceled December 2025). Company organized as a REIT; had zero revenue at IPO. Investment: equipment financing commitments exceed $600M ($500M MUFG turbine warehouse + $200M Keystone/Cape facility); projected total project cost $70–90B is a range/projection, not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Jobs: 50,000+ projected across campus lifetime — projection only, omitted from jobs field. Nuclear campus name in NRC COLA filings: 'President Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus'; publicly marketed as Project Matador / HyperGrid.

tcdc-ector-county-tx.name: Texas Critical Data Centers (TCDC)
tcdc-ector-county-tx.developer: Sharon AI + New Era Energy & Digital (joint venture)
tcdc-ector-county-tx.source: TCDC signs LOI to acquire an additional 203 acres for off-grid data center campus in Ector County, Texas
tcdc-ector-county-tx.notes: Potential to scale beyond 1GW (ceiling, not a confirmed committed figure). Power partners Thunderhead Energy Solutions and Mawgan Capital (behind-the-meter gas generation); GlobeLink providing dark fiber. Phased: first 100MW segment targeted online by December 2026, remaining 150MW roughly 6 months later. Coordinates are approximate (Odessa area).

creekstone-delta-ut.name: Creekstone Energy Delta Gigasite
creekstone-delta-ut.powered_by: On-site natural gas + utility-scale solar (SITLA lease) + nuclear planned
creekstone-delta-ut.water_notes: Dry cooling design described as 'essentially waterless operation'
creekstone-delta-ut.source: Zeo Energy to supply 280MW for Creekstone's 10GW Delta Gigasite
creekstone-delta-ut.notes: Claims to be world's largest planned AI data center campus at 20M sq ft. 1,143 acres owned; 13,000-acre SITLA lease for solar (largest solar lease in Utah history — record previously stated 30,000 acres, corrected to 13,000 acres per March 2026 BusinessWire announcement and multiple independent sources). Initial customer BluSky AI allocated up to 50MW. Adjacent to Intermountain Power Project. 10GW is full-buildout target; first 300MW gas delivery H1 2027. Coordinates at Delta city centroid; site is southeast of Delta.

anchorstone-58-east-data-campus-ringgold.name: 58 East Data Campus (Route 58 East Data Center Campus)
anchorstone-58-east-data-campus-ringgold.source: Pittsylvania County Board of Supervisors rezoning approval (7/16/2024) + Board of Zoning Appeals Special Use Permit approval
anchorstone-58-east-data-campus-ringgold.notes: Also referred to in some coverage as 'Route 58 East Data Center Campus'. Board of Zoning Appeals granted the Special Use Permit under the county's new M-2 heavy-industrial data-center-by-SUP ordinance (adopted May 21, 2024). Construction of phase 1 targeted mid-2025 to early 2026 per developer statements at time of approval; up to ~5 buildings, 200MW with room for expansion, ~$4-5B projected investment, build-out over ~10 years. Coordinates are town-centroid for Ringgold, VA (approximate) — exact parcel not geocoded from a parcel ID in sources reviewed this session. Pittsylvania County's first data-center rezoning (~945 ac off US-58, Ringgold), approved 2024 per Cardinal News; ~$5B investment and ~200 MW are reported estimates from secondary coverage (not in the primary) — omitted as structured figures pending a county case doc.

cleanarc-ruther-glen-va.name: CleanArc VA1
cleanarc-ruther-glen-va.water_notes: The Caroline County performance agreement prohibits potable water for industrial cooling (county water for washing/flushing only); closed-loop recirculation with initial water brought off-site. Not yet operational - no daily-use figure.
cleanarc-ruther-glen-va.source: CleanArc gets green light for data center campus in Caroline County, Virginia
cleanarc-ruther-glen-va.notes: 900 MW flagship campus in Ruther Glen, Caroline County, phased into the mid-2030s (200 MW online targeted Q3 2026). Distinct operator/parcel from the AWS Mattermeade campus (also Caroline County). Coordinates are the Ruther Glen area centroid. investmentUsd records the confirmed $3B first-phase pledge (VEDP); the ~$8.8B full-buildout figure is a projection and is excluded.

google-arcola-loudoun-va.name: Google Arcola Data Center (Loudoun County)
google-arcola-loudoun-va.source: Google Dulles / Arcola Center — 42575 Arcola Blvd, Sterling VA, fully operational, built 2020
google-arcola-loudoun-va.notes: Google data center at 42575 Arcola Blvd in the Arcola area of Loudoun County (Northern Virginia 'Data Center Alley') — the ~91-acre 'Arcola Center' parcel was purchased in 2017 for $58M (a land cost, not total capex), and the ARA1A building is operational (built 2020 per baxtel). DISTINCT from Google's tracked Chester and Midlothian (Richmond-area) Virginia campuses. No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the disclosed Arcola Blvd address; a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

lavue-massaponax-tech-campus-spotsylvani.name: Massaponax Tech Campus
lavue-massaponax-tech-campus-spotsylvani.source: Spotsylvania County official case page — R25-0004 Massaponax Tech Campus
lavue-massaponax-tech-campus-spotsylvani.notes: Distinct NEW campus, not a dup of tracked Cosner or PowerHouse 95. County case R25-0004; the 4th-submission Voluntary Proffer Statement (county DocumentCenter PDF, parsed locally) names Applicant 'Lavue Lane Owner LLC' (a Delaware LLC), Owner per Exhibit A, and 12 tax parcels (37-A-41, 37-A-41G, 37-A-44, 36-5-A1, 36-5-B1, 51-A-1A, 51-A-3, 37-A-41H, 37-A-42, 37-A-46, 37-A-45, 36-5-A) totaling 588.5564 acres, rezoning RU->I-2 for up to ~6.1M sq ft of data-center buildings (Phase 1 ~1.5M, Phase 2 ~4.5M) off Massaponax Church Rd / Mills Rd (US-17), Berkeley voting / Lee Hill magisterial district.

stack-stafford-technology-campus-va.name: Stafford Technology Campus
stack-stafford-technology-campus-va.source: Stafford County Zoning Reclassification case — data center
stack-stafford-technology-campus-va.notes: 523.94 acres, up to 23 buildings, 5.8-7.9M sq ft, six 300MW substations; rezoning approved Sept 2025.

tallgrass-project-jade-cheyenne-wy.name: Project Tembo
tallgrass-project-jade-cheyenne-wy.powered_by: On-site natural gas (Tallgrass Cheyenne Power Hub)
tallgrass-project-jade-cheyenne-wy.source: Crusoe gets go-ahead for 1.8GW data center campus and power plant in Cheyenne, Wyoming
tallgrass-project-jade-cheyenne-wy.notes: Switchgrass Industrial Park, Hwy 85 south of Cheyenne, Laramie County - geographically distinct from Meta (Project Cosmo) and Microsoft's Cheyenne campuses. 716-acre campus. Originally announced at 1.8GW as 'Project Jade' with an undisclosed hyperscale client (Crusoe Energy as builder); Crusoe exited June 2026. On 2026-07-08, Google was publicly revealed as owner/operator via subsidiary Jupiter Star Holdings, and the project was renamed 'Project Tembo'; capacity confirmed at 2.7GW with an ultimate ceiling of up to 10GW. The Cheyenne Power Hub on-site natural-gas plant supplies power (Tallgrass Energy; Black Hills Energy co-invested). ~$50B total project figure remains a projection. Completion targeted 2031.
